/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/highlights.source_en: **2.1 km cape trail** (~30 min, only 14 m gain) — wheelchair/stroller-friendly stretches
**Bangdupo Lighthouse** — octagonal, **flashes every 4 sec**, atop Bulgeun Oreum red volcanic cone
**Hyeopja Yeondae Beacon Fire Station** — 4 m × 9 m Joseon yeondae, **Special Monument No. 23-2**
**Tadao Ando architecture** — Glass House restaurant + Yumin Art Gallery (Phoenix Island)
**Seonbawi (Seon Rock)** — 10 m offshore volcanic neck, dragon king's youngest son legend
**FREE cape admission**; Yumin Art Gallery + Glass House separately ticketed
⟦G0⟧ **clearly visible 4 km north** from the cape tip — perfect Triple-UNESCO panorama backdrop

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G1⟧ works especially well in a small group** because the pace can be adjusted for wind, photos, coffee, or a short gallery stop when time and opening conditions allow. The coastal path gives open views toward ⟦G0⟧, while the lighthouse and Tadao Ando-related architecture add a clean visual contrast to the volcanic scenery. The guide can keep the visit focused on the parts guests care about most instead of moving everyone through at a fixed coach-tour pace.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G1⟧ (섭지코지)** is a narrow volcanic cape on Jeju's east coast. In Jeju dialect, **koji** means a cape or headland, and the place is known for open sea views, a gentle coastal path, the white lighthouse, and the broad view back toward ⟦G0⟧. The walk is scenic without being a heavy hike, so it works well for cruise guests who want strong photos and fresh sea air without spending the whole day climbing. Depending on time, guests may also see the Glass House area and the Yumin Art Museum exterior, both associated with architect Tadao Ando. The visit is kept flexible because wind, rain, gallery hours, and group walking speed can affect how much of the cape is covered.

**Jeju Black Pork BBQ** (Natural Monument 2015) or **Galchi Jorim** (braised hairtail)

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The small-group lunch stop gives guests a calmer mid-day break.** A guide-vetted East Jeju restaurant is chosen based on the day's timing, group preference, and opening conditions. The guide can help with menu translation and local dish recommendations, including black pork, seafood, or vegetarian-friendly options when arranged in advance. The longer lunch pace also gives the route a useful buffer if the morning stops take more time for photos or walking.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/3/descriptio.source_en: **East Jeju lunch stop** at a guide-vetted local restaurant in the Seongsan / Seongeup / Pyoseon area, chosen to fit cruise day-trip timing. **Two typical options**, selected based on group preference and availability: **(1) Jeju Black Pork Heukdwaeji BBQ** (제주 흑돼지) — Jeju's signature ingredient, the indigenous Black Pig was designated **Natural Monument of Korea** in 2015, and pork-belly cuts are grilled over charcoal at the table with traditional banchan; or **(2) Galchi Jorim** (갈치조림 — braised hairtail with radish, soy-chili sauce) — eastern Jeju's famous seafood dish, drawing on the daily catch from Seongsan and Seongeup-area harbors. Vegetarian options are available at most venues with advance notice (the guide confirms with the restaurant ~30 min ahead). Lunch duration is **~60 minutes**, fitting the cruise day-trip's tight timeline (full day usually 8 hours port-to-port). Beverages: barley tea (free), local **Jeju Beer** (~₩6,000), or **Hallasan Soju** (Jeju's signature distilled spirit, ~₩5,000). All restaurants in the rotation accept **major cards (Visa/Mastercard) + cash KRW**; bilingual photo menus (English/Chinese) are standard at the cruise-tour-vetted venues. Lunch is **NOT included** in the standard cruise tour pricing — typical out-of-pocket is **₩15,000–25,000 per person** (varies by dish); inclusive lunch upgrade available on booking.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/4/highlights.source_en: **Founded 1423** by Sejong the Great — administrative center until **1914 (~500 years)**
**110 traditional structures** within original eupseong walled-town footprint
**Important Folklore Cultural Heritage of South Korea** (entire village + multiple buildings)
**Two ~600-year-old trees** at center: Saw-leaf Zelkova + Japanese Hackberry — **Natural Monuments**
Designed on **Joseon Korean feng shui (geomancy) principles** — typical county-capital plan
**'Dae Jang Geum' (MBC 2003–2004)** filming location — international K-drama hit
**Omegisul (오메기술)** — rice-based Jeju liquor brewed by single family for generations (free tasting)
Historical scars: **1826 fire** destroyed ~80 buildings; **1948 Jeju Uprising** damage
**FREE admission** — village still inhabited by ~250 families maintaining traditions
